prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1494; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Reviewed the first notice of loss. Insured reports a collision at an intersection while turning left. Insured states the other vehicle was approaching from the opposite direction. No injuries reported at scene by insured. Photos requested.

Entry 2: Spoke with claimant by phone. Claimant reports neck pain and stiffness the morning after the collision and has since visited an urgent care clinic. Claimant is not represented by an attorney and prefers to handle the claim directly. Explained the claims process and requested medical records and treatment notes.

Entry 3: Received police report. Report notes the insured was turning left and the claimant was proceeding straight through the intersection. Citation issued to insured for failure to yield. Liability appears probable against insured pending review of scene photos and witness statements.

Entry 4: Claimant provided treatment summary. Diagnosis is whiplash-type cervical strain with recommended physical therapy over several weeks. Claimant reports ongoing headaches and difficulty turning head to the right while driving. Claimant has not yet returned to regular work duties. Medical bills are being reviewed against policy coverage.

Entry 5: Reviewed photos and vehicle damage estimate. Damage consistent with a rear quarter impact to claimant's vehicle. Claimant's vehicle is at repair facility and a supplement is expected. Injury evaluation remains open pending completion of physical therapy and an updated treatment report. Next follow-up scheduled to confirm treatment progress with claimant.
